# Hamiltonian Flow

For a Hamiltonian \(H\), its Hamiltonian vector field acts on a phase-space function by \(X_H[F]=\{F,H\}\). In an external-time model, the total derivative of an explicitly time-dependent observable \(F(q,p,t)\) along the resulting trajectory is \(dF/dt=\{F,H\}+\partial F/\partial t\). A constraint can also generate a bracket flow, but that curve may be gauge flow rather than external-time evolution.

Learn more: [Hamiltonian Phase Space and Poisson Brackets](../mathematics/hamiltonian-phase-space-and-poisson-brackets.md).
